subject.title: fix(cron): pin the cron webhook bearer token to operator-allowlisted hosts

question: Should existing `cron.webhookToken` configurations fail closed until an operator explicitly adds `cron.webhookTokenHosts`, or should the legacy attach-to-any-host behavior remain the default during an upgrade window?
rationale: The implementation correctly makes the credential and destination inseparable, but choosing immediate protection over backward-compatible bearer delivery is a user-impacting security-policy decision that code review cannot make unilaterally.

options.title: Adopt fail-closed rollout
options.body: Merge the current behavior: withhold the token until operators name trusted hosts or explicitly choose `*`, while preserving delivery and Doctor guidance.

options.title: Stage compatibility
options.body: Keep legacy attachment when no allowlist is configured and add an explicit strict mode or future deprecation path, accepting continued exposure until that transition completes.

recommendation.title: Adopt fail-closed rollout
recommendation.body: Merge the current behavior: withhold the token until operators name trusted hosts or explicitly choose `*`, while preserving delivery and Doctor guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: They have implemented and documented both rollout shapes and can make the small localized adjustment once the policy direction is chosen.
